entries.title: Abu Nuwas (crater)
entries.extract: Abu Nuwas is an impact crater on the planet Mercury. It is named after the Arab poet Abu Nuwas, and its name was approved by the International Astronomical Union in 1976. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Adventure Rupes
entries.extract: Adventure Rupes is an escarpment on Mercury approximately 270 kilometres long located in the southern hemisphere of Mercury. Discovered by the Mariner 10 spacecraft in 1974, it was formed by a thrust fault, thought to have occurred due to the shrinkage of the planet's core as it cooled over time.

entries.title: Africanus Horton (crater)
entries.extract: Africanus Horton is a circular impact crater on Mercury. It was named by the IAU in 1976, after Africanus Horton, a Creole African nationalist writer and an esteemed medical surgeon in the British Army from Freetown, Sierra Leone.

entries.title: Aristoxenus (crater)

entries.title: Aśvaghoṣa (crater)
entries.extract: Aśvaghoṣa is an impact crater on Mercury. It is a nearly circular formation, and its rim remains intact, except where it is broken at its southern side, and at its northern side by an indentation from two conjoined craters.

entries.title: Bashō (crater)
entries.extract: Bashō is a crater on Mercury named after Matsuo Bashō, a 17th-century Japanese writer.37 mi) in diameter, but is a prominent feature on Mercury's surface, due to its bright rays. entries.title: Caloris Montes
entries.extract: The Caloris Montes are a range of mountains on Mercury. They are a system of linear hills and valleys that extend more than 1000 km to the northeast from the mountainous rim of Caloris Basin in the Shakespeare quadrangle (H-3).

entries.title: Caloris Planitia
entries.extract: Caloris Planitia is a plain within a large impact basin on Mercury, informally named Caloris, about 1,550 km (960 mi) in diameter. It is one of the largest impact basins in the Solar System.

entries.extract: Jókai is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. Jokai is named for the Hungarian novelist Mór Jókai, who lived from 1825 to 1904.

entries.title: Keats (crater)
entries.extract: Keats is a crater on Mercury. The crater's name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976 and named after an English poet. This poet is known as John Keats, who lived from 1795 to 1821. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Kenkō (crater)
entries.extract: Kenkō is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Kenko is named for the Japanese author Yoshida Kenkō, who lived from 1283 to 1352. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Khansa (crater)
entries.extract: Khansa is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Khansa is named after the Arab poet al-Khansa, who lived in the 6th century CE.

entries.title: Kuan Han-Chʻing (crater)
entries.extract: Kuan Han-Chʻing is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1979. Kuan Han-Chʻing is named for the Chinese playwright Guan Hanqing, who lived from 1241 to 1320. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Kuiper (Mercurian crater)
entries.extract: 23°W on Mercury. It is 62 kilometers in diameter and was named after Dutch-American astronomer Gerard Kuiper in 1976. It is one of only 2 Mercurian craters which are named not after artists, and one of very few cases when the same name is used for 3 craters.

entries.title: Kurosawa (crater)
entries.extract: Kurosawa is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Kurosawa is named for the Japanese composer Kinko Kurosawa, who lived in the 18th century CE.

entries.title: Kālidāsā (crater)
entries.extract: Kālidāsā is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976. Kalidasa is named for the Indian writer Kālidāsa, who lived in the 5th century CE.

entries.title: Kōshō (crater)
entries.extract: Kōshō is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1985. Kōshō is named for the Japanese sculptor Kōshō, who lived in the 13th century CE.

entries.title: Leopardi (crater)
entries.extract: Leopardi is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976. Leopardi is named for the Italian writer Giacomo Leopardi, who lived from 1798 to 1837 from the crater.

entries.title: Lermontov (crater)
entries.extract: Lermontov is an impact crater on the planet Mercury. The crater is named after Mikhail Yuryevich Lermontov, a 19th-century Russian poet. The name was approved by the International Astronomical Union in 1976.

entries.title: Lessing (crater)
entries.extract: Lessing is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1985. Lessing is named for the German writer Gotthold Ephraim Lessing, who lived from 1729 to 1781.

entries.title: Li Chʻing-Chao (crater)
entries.extract: Li Chʻing-Chao is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 61 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Li Chʻing-Chao is named for the Chinese poet Li Qingzhao, who lived from 1081 to c. 1141.

entries.title: Li Po (crater)
entries.extract: Li Po is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 120 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Li Po is named for the Chinese poet Li Bai, who lived from 701 to 762.

entries.title: Liang Kʻai (crater)
entries.extract: Liang Kʻai is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 140 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1979. Liang Kʻai is named for the Chinese artist Liang Kai, who lived from 1140 to 1210.

entries.title: Liszt (crater)
entries.extract: Liszt is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 85 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1985. Liszt is named for the Hungarian composer Franz Liszt, who lived from 1811 to 1886.

entries.title: Lu Hsun (crater)
entries.extract: Lu Hsun is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 98 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Lu Hsun is named for the Chinese writer Lu Hsun, who lived from 1881 to 1936.

entries.title: Lysippus (crater)
entries.extract: Lysippus is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976. Lysippus is named for the Greek sculptor Lysippos, who lived in the 4th century BCE. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Ma Chih-Yuan (crater)
entries.extract: Ma Chih-Yuan is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Ma Chih-Yuan is named for the Chinese playwright Ma Zhiyuan, who lived in the 13th century CE.

entries.title: Machaut (crater)
entries.extract: Machaut is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976. Machaut is named for the French composer and poet Guillaume de Machaut, who lived from 1300 to 1377. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Mahler (crater)
entries.extract: Mahler is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 103 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Mahler is named for the Austrian composer Gustav Mahler, who lived from 1860 to 1911. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Mansart (crater)
entries.extract: Mansart is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. Mansart is named for the French architect Jules Hardouin-Mansart, who lived from 1646 to 1708.

entries.title: Mansur (crater)
entries.extract: Mansur is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1979. Mansur is named for the Indian artist Ustad Mansur, who lived in the 17th century CE. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: March (crater)
entries.extract: March is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1979. March is named for the Valencian poet in Catalan language Ausias March, who lived from 1397 to 1459.

entries.title: Mark Twain (crater)
entries.extract: Mark Twain is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Mark Twain is named for the American author Mark Twain, who lived from 1835 to 1910.

entries.title: Martial (crater)
entries.extract: Martial is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 51 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1979. Martial is named for the ancient Roman poet Martial, who lived from 40 to 103. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Martí (crater)
entries.extract: Martí is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Martí is named for the Cuban writer José Martí, who lived from 1853 to 1895.

entries.title: Matisse (crater)
entries.extract: Matisse is an impact crater on the southern hemisphere of Mercury. Matisse takes its name from the French artist Henri Matisse, and it was named by the IAU in 1976.

entries.title: Melville (crater)
entries.extract: Melville is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 154 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Melville is named for the American novelist Herman Melville, who lived from 1819 to 1891.

entries.title: Mena (Mercurian crater)
entries.extract: Mena is a crater in the Beethoven quadrangle on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976. Mena is named for the Spanish poet Juan de Mena, who lived from 1411 to 1456.

entries.title: Mendes Pinto (crater)
entries.extract: Mendes Pinto is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Mendes Pinto is named for the Portuguese explorer and prose author Fernão Mendes Pinto, who lived from 1510 to 1583.

entries.title: Michelangelo (crater)
entries.extract: Michelangelo is a 230 km diameter impact basin in the Michelangelo quadrangle of Mercury, which is named after this crater. The crater itself was named by the IAU in 1979 after the Italian painter, sculptor and architect Michelangelo.

entries.title: Mickiewicz (crater)
entries.extract: Mickiewicz is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Mickiewicz is named for the Polish poet Adam Mickiewicz, who lived from 1798 to 1855.

entries.title: Milton (crater)
entries.extract: Milton is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 186 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976. Milton is named for the English poet John Milton, who lived from 1608 to 1674.

entries.title: Mistral (crater)
entries.extract: Mistral is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Mistral is named for the Chilean poet Gabriela Mistral, who lived from 1889 to 1957.

entries.title: Mofolo (crater)
entries.extract: Mofolo is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976. Mofolo is named for the Basotho writer Thomas Mofolo, who lived from 1876 or 1877 to 1948. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Molière (crater)
entries.extract: Molière is an impact crater on the planet Mercury. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974. The nearly circular rim of the crater is cut off into a flat edge on its southern and southwestern ends, and on its eastern side the rim is indented by a smaller crater.

entries.title: Monet (crater)
entries.extract: Monet is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. Monet is named for the French artist Claude Monet, who lived from 1840 to 1926. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Monteverdi (crater)
entries.extract: Monteverdi is a crater on Mercury with a diameter of 138 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979, from the Italian composer Claudio Monteverdi, a crucial transitional figure between Renaissance and Baroque music.

entries.title: Mozart (crater)
entries.extract: Mozart is a crater on Mercury, named by the IAU in 1976 after Austrian composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.

entries.title: Murasaki (crater)
entries.extract: Murasaki is a crater on Mercury located at 12 S, 31 W. It is 132 km in diameter. It was named after 10th-11th century Japanese writer Murasaki Shikibu. The name was approved by IAU's Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature in 1976. To its east lies the slightly larger Hiroshige.

entries.title: Mussorgskij (crater)
entries.extract: Mussorgskij is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. Mussorgskij is named for the Russian composer Modest Mussorgsky, who lived from 1839 to 1881. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Myron (crater)
entries.extract: Myron is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 31 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1979. Myron is named for the ancient Greek sculptor Myron, who lived from 480 to 440 BCE.

entries.title: Nampeyo (crater)
entries.extract: Nampeyo is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 52 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976. Nampeyo is named for the Hopi-Tewa ceramics artist Nampeyo, who lived from 1860 to 1942.

entries.title: Nervo (crater)
entries.extract: Nervo is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1979. Nervo is named for the Mexican poet Amado Nervo, who lived from 1870 to 1919. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Neumann (crater)
entries.extract: Neumann is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 120 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Neumann is named for the German architect Johann Balthasar Neumann, who lived from 1687 to 1753. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Nizāmī (crater)
entries.extract: Nizāmī is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. Nizami is named for the Persian poet Nizami Ganjavi, who lived from 1141 to 1209.

entries.title: Odin Planitia
entries.extract: Odin Planitia is a large basin on Mercury. It was named after the Norse god Odin, who was sometimes considered to be the equivalent of the Roman god Mercury, in 1976 by the IAU. It was first observed in detail by Mariner 10. The plain is approximately 473 kilometers in diameter.

entries.title: Ovid (crater)
entries.extract: Ovid is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Ovid is named for the Roman poet Ovid, who lived from 43 BCE to 17 CE.

entries.title: Petrarch (crater)
entries.extract: Petrarch is a crater on Mercury. This crater is located within the distorted terrain on the opposite side of the planet from the Caloris Basin. It was named after Petrarch, the medieval Italian poet, by the IAU in 1976.

entries.title: Phidias (crater)
entries.extract: Phidias is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Phidias is named for the Greek artist Phidias, who lived from 490 to 430 BCE. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Philoxenus (crater)
entries.extract: Philoxenus is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Philoxenus is named for Greek lyric poet Philoxenus of Cythera.

entries.title: Pigalle (crater)
entries.extract: Pigalle is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 153 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Pigalle is named for the French sculptor Jean-Baptiste Pigalle.

entries.title: Po Chü-I (crater)
entries.extract: Po Chü-I is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Po Chü-I is named for the Chinese poet Bai Juyi.

entries.title: Po Ya (crater)
entries.extract: Po Ya is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the IAU in 1976, after Bo Ya, a Chinese musician who lived in 8th century B.C. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Polygnotus (crater)
entries.extract: Polygnotus is a crater on Mercury, named by the IAU in 1976, after ancient Greek painter Polygnotus. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Praxiteles (crater)
entries.extract: Praxiteles is a crater on Mercury. It is one of 110 peak ring basins on Mercury.

entries.title: Proust (crater)
entries.extract: Proust is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. It is named after the French novelist Marcel Proust.

entries.title: Puccini (crater)
entries.extract: Puccini is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. It is named for the Italian composer Giacomo Puccini.

entries.title: Purcell (crater)
entries.extract: Purcell is a crater on Mercury, located near the north pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. It is named for the English composer Henry Purcell.

entries.title: Pushkin (crater)
entries.extract: Pushkin is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Pushkin is named after Russian poet Alexander Pushkin.

entries.title: Rabelais (crater)
entries.extract: Rabelais is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 154 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Rabelais is named for the French writer François Rabelais.

entries.title: Rajnis (crater)
entries.extract: Rajnis is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. The crater is named for the Latvian poet Jānis Pliekšāns, known by his pseudonym of Rainis.

entries.title: Rameau (crater)
entries.extract: Rameau is a crater on Mercury. It was named by the IAU in 1976, after French composer Jean Philippe Rameau.

entries.title: Raphael (crater)
entries.extract: Raphael is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976, and is named for the Italian painter Raphael. It is Tolstojan in age. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Ravel (crater)
entries.extract: Ravel is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1985, after the French composer Maurice Ravel.

entries.title: Renoir (crater)
entries.extract: Renoir is a crater on the planet Mercury. Its name, after the French painter Pierre-Auguste Renoir (1841–1919), was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976.

entries.title: Repin (crater)
entries.extract: Repin is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Repin is named for the Russian painter Ilya Repin. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Resolution Rupes
entries.extract: Resolution Rupes is an escarpment on Mercury approximately 190 kilometers long located in the southern hemisphere of Mercury. Discovered by the Mariner 10 spacecraft in 1974, it was formed by a thrust fault, thought to have occurred due to the shrinkage of the planet's core as it cooled over time.

entries.title: Riemenschneider (crater)
entries.extract: Riemenschneider is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. Riemenschneider is named for the German sculptor Tilman Riemenschneider. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Rilke (crater)
entries.extract: Rilke is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Rilke is named for the German poet Rainer Maria Rilke.

entries.title: Rimbaud (crater)
entries.extract: Rimbaud is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1985. Rimbaud is named for French poet Arthur Rimbaud. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Rodin (crater)
entries.extract: Rodin is an impact crater on the planet Mercury, 230 kilometers in diameter. The rim is even and circular, except where it is broken in two places toward the north and south. It is named for the French sculptor Auguste Rodin. Its name was approved by the International Astronomical Union in 1976.

entries.title: Rubens (crater)
entries.extract: Rubens is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979, after Flemish painter Peter Paul Rubens. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Rublev (crater)
entries.extract: Rublev is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Rublev is named for the Russian painter Andrei Rublev.

entries.title: Rude (crater)
entries.extract: Rude is an impact crater on the planet Mercury. It is named for the French sculptor François Rude. Its name was approved by the International Astronomical Union in 1985.

entries.title: Rūdaki (crater)
entries.extract: Rūdaki is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the IAU in 1976, after the Persian poet Rudaki. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Rūmī (crater)
entries.extract: Rūmī is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 75 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1985. Rūmī is named for the Persian poet Rumi.

entries.title: Sadī (crater)
entries.extract: Sadī is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976, after Persian poet Saadi Shirazi.

entries.title: Saikaku (crater)
entries.extract: Saikaku is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. The crater is named for Japanese poet Ihara Saikaku.

entries.title: Santa María Rupes
entries.extract: Santa María Rupes is a prominent lobate escarpment and fault line on Mercury. According to data from Arecibo, it has a relief of roughly 700m. The formation was named after the ship Santa María, used by Christopher Columbus. The escarpment was probably created as Mercury cooled and thus contracted.

entries.title: Sarmiento (crater)
entries.extract: Sarmiento is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979, and is named for the Argentine writer Domingo Faustino Sarmiento.

entries.title: Sayat-Nova (crater)
entries.extract: Sayat-Nova is an impact crater on the planet Mercury. It is named for the Armenian/Georgian song writer Aruthin Sayadian Sayat-Nova. Its name was approved by the International Astronomical Union in 1979. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Scarlatti (crater)
entries.extract: Scarlatti is a pit-floored crater on Mercury, which was discovered in 1974 by the Mariner 10 spacecraft. It has a prominent peak ring, and it is one of 110 peak ring basins on Mercury. The crater floor is covered by the smooth plains material.

entries.title: Schoenberg (crater)
entries.extract: Schoenberg is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. The crater is named for Austrian composer Arnold Schoenberg.

entries.title: Schubert (Mercurian crater)
entries.extract: Schubert is a crater on Mercury. It was named after Franz Schubert, a famous Austrian composer, by the IAU in 1976.

entries.title: Scopas (crater)
entries.extract: Scopas is a crater on Mercury, near the south pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976, after the ancient Greek sculptor and architect Scopas, following the official convention of naming craters on Mercury after historically significant artists, musicians, painters, and authors.

entries.title: Sei (crater)
entries.extract: Sei is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. The crater is named for Japanese writer Sei Shōnagon.

entries.title: Shakespeare (Mercurian crater)
entries.extract: Shakespeare is an impact basin in the Shakespeare quadrangle of Mercury, which is named after this crater. It was named after playwright William Shakespeare in 1979. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Shelley (crater)
entries.extract: Shelley is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the IAU in 1979, after the English poet Percy Bysshe Shelley, who lived from 1792 to 1822. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Shevchenko (crater)
entries.extract: Shevchenko is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976, for Ukrainian poet Taras Hryhorovych Shevchenko.

entries.title: Sholem Aleichem (crater)
entries.extract: Sholem Aleichem is a crater on Mercury, named after the Yiddish writer Sholem Aleichem in 1979. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Sibelius (crater)
entries.extract: Sibelius is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 94 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1985. Sibelius is named for the Finnish composer Jean Sibelius. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Simonides (crater)
entries.extract: Simonides is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1985. The crater is named for Greek lyric poet Simonides. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Sinan (crater)
entries.extract: Sinan is an impact crater on the planet Mercury, 134 kilometers in diameter. It is located northeast of the crater Yeats and southeast of the crater Li Po. It has one craterlet on the south-southwestern side of the crater floor, and it has a symmetrical pit slightly west of the center.

entries.title: Smetana (crater)
entries.extract: Smetana is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1985. The crater is named for Czech composer Bedřich Smetana.

entries.title: Snorri (crater)
entries.extract: Snorri is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Snorri is named for the Icelandic poet Snorri Sturluson. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Sobkou Planitia
entries.extract: Sobkou Planitia is a large basin on the planet Mercury. It is named after the ancient Egyptian messenger deity Sobkou. He was associated by the Egyptians with the planet Mercury.

entries.title: Sophocles (crater)
entries.extract: Sophocles is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976, after the Greek dramatist Sophocles.

entries.title: Sor Juana (crater)
entries.extract: Sor Juana is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979, and is named for the Mexican writer and poet Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Spitteler (crater)
entries.extract: Spitteler is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. It is named for the Swiss epic poet Carl Spitteler.

entries.title: Stravinsky (crater)
entries.extract: Stravinsky is a crater on Mercury. It overlays the rim of the much older Vyāsa crater. It was named by the IAU in 1979 for the influential Russian composer Igor Stravinsky. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Strindberg (crater)
entries.extract: Strindberg is a 189 km diameter impact basin in the Shakespeare quadrangle of Mercury. It was named after the Swedish playwright, novelist and short story writer August Strindberg.

entries.title: Suisei Planitia
entries.extract: Suisei Planitia is a large area of smooth plains on Mercury, approximately 570 km wide. Ghost craters are unusual forms that occur in the Suisei Planitia. They are buried and rounded in profile, with only their rim crests rising above the surrounding smooth plains.

entries.title: Sullivan (Mercurian crater)
entries.extract: Sullivan is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976, and is named for the American architect Louis Sullivan. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Surikov (crater)
entries.extract: Surikov is a crater on the planet Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. Surikov is named for the Russian painter Vasily Surikov. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Sōseki (crater)
entries.extract: Sōseki is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1985. The crater is named for Japanese novelist Natsume Sōseki. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Sōtatsu (crater)
entries.extract: Sōtatsu is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the IAU in 1976, after the Japanese artist Tawaraya Sōtatsu. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Sūr Dās (crater)
entries.extract: Sūr Dās is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. The crater is named for the Indian poet Surdas. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Takanobu (crater)
entries.extract: Takanobu is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1985. The crater is named for Japanese poet and portrait artist Fujiwara no Takanobu. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Takayoshi (crater)
entries.extract: Takayoshi is an impact crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the IAU in 1979.

entries.title: Tansen (crater)
entries.extract: Tansen is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. The crater is named for Tansen, Mughal composer from the court of Akbar. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Theophanes (crater)
entries.extract: Theophanes is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the IAU in 1976, after the Byzantine painter Theophanes.

entries.title: Thoreau (crater)
entries.extract: Thoreau is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1985, after American poet and philosopher Henry David Thoreau. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Thākur (crater)
entries.extract: Thākur is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 111 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Thākur is named for the Indian writer Rabindranath Tagore. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Tintoretto (crater)
entries.extract: Tintoretto is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the IAU in 1976, after the Italian painter Tintoretto. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Tir Planitia
entries.extract: Tir Planitia is a large plain on the planet Mercury. The name Tir (تیر) is the Persian word for "Mercury", and the name was approved in 1976. It was first observed in detail by Mariner 10. It lies between the large crater Mozart and the ancient Tolstoj basin.

entries.title: Titian (crater)
entries.extract: Titian is an impact crater on the planet Mercury. It was named by the IAU in 1976.

entries.title: Tolstoj (crater)
entries.extract: Tolstoj is a large, ancient impact crater on Mercury. It was named after Leo Tolstoy by the IAU in 1976. The albedo feature Solitudo Maiae appears to be associated with this crater.

entries.title: Tsurayuki (crater)
entries.extract: Tsurayuki is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Tsurayuki is named for Japanese author, poet, and courtier Ki no Tsurayuki.

entries.title: Tsʻai Wen-Chi (crater)
entries.extract: Tsʻai Wen-Chi is an impact crater on the planet Mercury. It is located northwest of the larger Rodin crater. It is named for the Chinese composer Cai Yan. Its name was approved by the International Astronomical Union in 1976. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Tsʻao Chan (crater)
entries.extract: Tsʻao Chan is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976, for the Chinese writer Tsʻao Chan.

entries.title: Tung Yüan (crater)
entries.extract: Tung Yüan is a crater on Mercury, within the Borealis Planitia. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1979, for the 10th century Chinese painter Tung Yüan.

entries.title: Turgenev (crater)
entries.extract: Turgenev is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. The crater is named for Russian writer Ivan Sergeyevich Turgenev.

entries.title: Tyagaraja (crater)
entries.extract: Tyagaraja is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976. Tyagaraja is named for the Indian composer Tyagaraja. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Unkei (crater)
entries.extract: Unkei is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976, after the Japanese sculptor Unkei.

entries.title: Ustad Isa (crater)
entries.extract: Ustad Isa is an impact crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the IAU in 1979.

entries.title: Van Dijck (crater)
entries.extract: Van Dijck is a crater on Mercury, located near the north pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. Van Dijck is named for Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck.

entries.title: Van Eyck (crater)
entries.extract: Van Eyck is a 271 km diameter impact basin in the Shakespeare quadrangle of Mercury. It is named after the 15th century Flemish painter Jan van Eyck. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Van Gogh (crater)
entries.extract: Van Gogh is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Van Gogh is named for the Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh.

entries.title: Velázquez (crater)
entries.extract: Velázquez is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 128 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. Velázquez is named for the Spanish painter Diego Velázquez. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Verdi (crater)
entries.extract: Verdi is an impact crater on the planet Mercury. It was named after Italian Romantic composer Giuseppe Verdi (1813–1901) in 1979, as recognized by the International Astronomical Union. The crater's extensive ejecta blanket and secondary crater field are superposed on plains materials and older craters.

entries.title: Victoria Rupes
entries.extract: Victoria Rupes is an escarpment in the Victoria quadrangle of Mercury. The quadrangle was named after this escarpment, and the escarpment itself was named after the Victoria, a ship used on the famous expedition of Ferdinand Magellan. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976.

entries.title: Vincente (crater)
entries.extract: Vicente is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 108 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. Vicente is named for the Portuguese writer Gil Vicente. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Vivaldi (crater)
entries.extract: Vivaldi is a crater on Mercury. It was named by the IAU after Italian composer Antonio Vivaldi in 1976. It has a prominent and nearly continuous inner ring whose diameter measures about half that of the outer ring. It is one of 110 peak ring basins on Mercury.

entries.title: Vlaminck (crater)
entries.extract: Vlaminck is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 82 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1985. Vlaminck is named for the French painter Maurice de Vlaminck. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Vostok Rupes
entries.extract: Vostok Rupes is an escarpment on Mercury. The scarp is a surface manifestation of a thrust fault, which formed when the planet contracted as its interior cooled.

entries.title: Vyāsa (crater)
entries.extract: Vyāsa is a crater on Mercury. It was named by the IAU in 1979, after the Hindu poet Vyasa. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Vālmiki (crater)
entries.extract: Vālmiki is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. It is named for the Indian poet Valmiki.

entries.title: Wagner (crater)
entries.extract: Wagner is an impact crater in the south polar region of the planet Mercury. It was named after the German composer Richard Wagner (1813–1883) in 1976, as recognized by the International Astronomical Union. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Wang Meng (crater)
entries.extract: Wang Meng is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. The crater is named for the Chinese painter Wang Meng.

entries.title: Wergeland (crater)
entries.extract: Wergeland is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976, after the Norwegian poet Henrik Arnold Wergeland.

entries.title: Whitman (crater)
entries.extract: Whitman is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1985. Whitman is named for American poet Walt Whitman. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Wren (crater)
entries.extract: Wren is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 204 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1979. Wren is named for English architect Christopher Wren. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Yeats (crater)
entries.extract: Yeats is an impact crater on the planet Mercury. It is named after William Butler Yeats, an Irish poet and dramatist. The name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976.

entries.title: Yun Sŏn-Do (crater)
entries.extract: Yun Sŏn-Do is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 76 kilometres (47 mi). Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1976. Yun Sŏn-Do is named for the Korean poet Yun Sŏndo.

entries.title: Zeami (crater)
entries.extract: Zeami is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1976, after the Japanese dramatist and playwright Zeami Motokiyo.

entries.title: Zola (crater)
entries.extract: Zola is a crater on Mercury, first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974. The crater was named after the French novelist and playwright Émile Zola by the IAU in 1979.

entries.title: Ōkyo (crater)
entries.extract: Ōkyo is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 1985. It is named for the Japanese painter Maruyama Ōkyo, who lived from 1733 to 1795.

entries.title: Raditladi (crater)
entries.extract: Raditladi is a large impact crater on Mercury with a diameter of 263 km. Inside its peak ring there is a system of concentric extensional troughs (graben), which are rare surface features on Mercury.

entries.title: Eminescu (crater)
entries.extract: Eminescu is a peak ring crater on Mercury 125 kilometers (78 mi) in diameter. Since there are very few later craters superposed on it, Eminescu appears to be a young crater formed around one billion years ago.

entries.title: Sveinsdóttir (crater)
entries.extract: Sveinsdóttir is a large, elongated impact crater on Mercury. Its dimensions are 220 × 120 km.

entries.title: Beagle Rupes
entries.extract: Beagle Rupes is an escarpment on Mercury, one of the highest and longest yet seen. It was discovered in 2008 when MESSENGER made its first flyby of the planet. It has an arcuate shape and is about 600 kilometres (370 mi) long.

entries.title: Neruda (crater)
entries.extract: Neruda is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 112 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2008. Neruda was formerly named for the Chilean poet Pablo Neruda, who lived from 1904 to 1973.

entries.title: Xiao Zhao (crater)
entries.extract: Xiao Zhao crater is small in comparison with many other craters on Mercury. However, Xiao Zhao's long bright rays make it a readily visible feature.

entries.title: Cunningham (crater)
entries.extract: Cunningham is a young crater on the western floor of the Caloris Basin, on Mercury. It is surrounded by a bright ray system.

entries.title: Atget (crater)
entries.extract: Atget crater is distinctive on the planet Mercury's surface due to its dark color. Atget crater is located within Caloris basin, near Apollodorus crater and Pantheon Fossae.

entries.title: Sander (crater)
entries.extract: Sander is a crater on Mercury within Caloris Basin. It has dark walls and bright patches on its floor. Unlike the rays of Bashō crater, the bright areas are not believed to be immature, but they are inherently bright. It is named after the German photographer August Sander (1876–1964).

entries.title: Pantheon Fossae
entries.extract: The Pantheon Fossae are a radial set of troughs in a region in the middle of Caloris Basin on Mercury. They appear to be a set of graben formed by extensional faults, with a 40 km crater located near the center of the pattern. The exact origin of this pattern of troughs is not currently known.

entries.title: Apollodorus (crater)
entries.extract: Apollodorus is an impact crater on Mercury. Its unusual appearance, with radiating dark troughs, led to a nickname of "the Spider" by scientists before its official name was decided.

entries.title: Kertész (crater)
entries.extract: Located in the western edge of Mercury's giant Caloris basin, Kertész crater has some unusual, bright material located on its floor. Sander crater, located in the northwestern edge of Caloris basin, also shows bright material on its floor.

entries.title: Amaral (crater)
entries.extract: Amaral is a crater on the planet Mercury. With its smooth floor, surrounding ejecta, and small secondary craters, it appears noticeably younger than the heavily cratered surface around it. Along with a smooth crater floor, Amaral also has a central peak.

entries.title: Dali (crater)
entries.extract: Dali is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 176 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2008. Dali is named for the Spanish painter Salvador Dalí (1904-1989).

entries.title: Enwonwu (crater)
entries.extract: Enwonwu is an impact crater on the planet Mercury. It is named in honor of Ben Enwonwu, the modernist Nigerian sculptor and painter. The crater displays a central peak and a set of bright rays emanating from the crater rim.

entries.title: Glinka (crater)
entries.extract: Glinka is a pit-floored crater on Mercury, which was discovered in 1974 by Mariner 10 spacecraft. It was named by the IAU in 2008, after Russian composer Mikhail Glinka.

entries.title: Hovnatanian (crater)
entries.extract: Hovnatanian is a crater on Mercury. Its “butterfly” pattern of ejecta rays were created by an impact at an even lower angle than that which formed neighboring Qi Baishi crater.

entries.title: Beckett (crater)
entries.extract: Beckett is a pit-floored crater on Mercury, which was discovered in January 2008 during the first flyby of the planet by the MESSENGER spacecraft. The crater was named in November 2008 by the IAU, after Australian artist Clarice Beckett.

entries.title: Moody (crater)
entries.extract: Moody is an impact crater on Mercury.

entries.title: Munch (crater)
entries.extract: Munch is a crater on Mercury. It was discovered on the first flyby of Mercury by the MESSENGER spacecraft on 14 January 2008, and was named after Edvard Munch a Norwegian painter, printmaker, and draftsman (1863-1944) by the IAU in November of the same year.

entries.title: Navoi (crater)
entries.extract: Navoi is a crater on Mercury. It contains uncommon reddish material that indicates a different rock composition from its surroundings. Navoi also appears to have an irregularly shaped depression in its center.

entries.title: Nāwahī (crater)
entries.extract: Nāwahī is a crater on Mercury. Nāwahī crater is located within the large Caloris basin, near the western rim.

entries.title: Oskison (crater)
entries.extract: The crater Oskison is located in the far northern hemisphere of Mercury, in the plains north of Caloris basin. Oskison is a distinctive crater with a large central peak that exposes material excavated from depth.

entries.title: Poe (crater)
entries.extract: Poe is a crater on Mercury. It has diameter about 77 km (48 mi) and is situated in northern part of Caloris Planitia.

entries.title: Qi Baishi (crater)
entries.extract: Qi Baishi is a crater on Mercury. The crater was named after famed Chinese painter Qi Baishi. The crater has an asymmetric pattern of ejecta rays, which formed by an object traveling to the east or to the west and impacting Mercury's surface at a very low incidence angle.

entries.title: Raden Saleh (crater)
entries.extract: Raden Saleh is a crater on Mercury. Its name was approved by the IAU in 2008, and it is named after a famous Indonesian painter named Raden Saleh.

entries.title: Sher-Gil (crater)
entries.extract: Sher-Gil is a crater on Mercury, named by the International Astronomical Union in 2016 after the Indian painter Amrita Sher-Gil. Hollows are present. To its southwest is Neruda crater.

entries.title: Rembrandt (crater)
entries.extract: Rembrandt is a large impact crater on Mercury. With a diameter of 716 km it is the second-largest impact basin on the planet, after Caloris, and is one of the larger craters in the Solar System. It was discovered by MESSENGER during its second flyby of Mercury on October 6, 2008.

entries.title: Abedin (crater)
entries.extract: Abedin is a crater on Mercury. It was named after the Bangladeshi artist Zainul Abedin by the IAU in 2009.

entries.title: Benoit (crater)
entries.extract: Benoit is a crater on Mercury. Its floor is quite unusual, with two mounds that have been suggested to be evidence of intrusive volcanic activity on Mercury.

entries.title: Berkel (crater)
entries.extract: Berkel is a crater on the planet Mercury. Its name was approved by the IAU on July 9, 2009. It was named after the modernist painter Sabri Berkel.

entries.title: Calvino (crater)
entries.extract: Calvino is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the IAU in 2016, after the Italian writer Italo Calvino. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: De Graft (crater)
entries.extract: De Graft is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2009, after Ghanaian playwright, poet, and novelist Joe de Graft.

entries.title: Derain (crater)
entries.extract: Derain is a crater on Mercury named after André Derain, a French artist, painter, sculptor and co-founder of Fauvism with Henri Matisse. It has uncommonly dark material within and surrounding the crater.

entries.title: Eastman (crater)
entries.extract: Eastman is a crater on Mercury first seen by MESSENGER during the mission's first Mercury flyby. Eastman exhibits some features characteristic of a fresh, relatively young crater. The walls of Eastman have clearly visible terraces, and the central peak structure is well preserved.

entries.title: Gibran (crater)
entries.extract: Gibran is a crater on Mercury and is in the east of the Shakespeare quadrangle. It was named after Lebanese-American poet Khalil Gibran in 2009. Gibran is located east of the rayed crater of Degas and nearby Damer.

entries.title: Hemingway (crater)
entries.extract: Hemingway is a crater on Mercury. It has a patch of very dark material located near its center. The dark color is likely due to rocks that have a different mineralogical composition from that of the surrounding surface.

entries.title: Hodgkins (crater)
entries.extract: Hodgkins is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 19 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2009. Hodgkins is named for the New Zealand painter Frances Hodgkins, who lived from 1869 to 1947.

entries.title: Izquierdo (crater)
entries.extract: Izquierdo is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2009, for the Mexican painter María Izquierdo. The floor of Izquierdo is smooth, the result of having been partially filled with volcanic lava.

entries.title: Kunisada (crater)
entries.extract: Kunisada is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 241 km (150 mi). Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2009. Kunisada is named for the Japanese woodblock printer Utagawa Kunisada, who lived from 1786 to 1864.

entries.title: Lange (crater)
entries.extract: Lange is a crater on Mercury. It was named by the IAU in 2009 after American photographer Dorothea Lange.

entries.title: Matabei (crater)
entries.extract: Matabei is an impact crater on Mercury. It has a set of dark rays. Dark rays are rare on Mercury, but other occurrences have been identified, such as at Mozart crater. Mozart crater is interpreted to have excavated dark material from depth during the impact event, creating dark streamers.

entries.title: Munkácsy (crater)
entries.extract: Munkácsy, named after Mihály Munkácsy, is a crater on Mercury. Munkácsy originally had a double-ring basin structure, but most of the inner ring was buried when the basin was flooded with volcanic lava.

entries.title: To Ngoc Van (crater)
entries.extract: To Ngoc Van is a pit-floored crater on Mercury, named after the Vietnamese artist Tô Ngọc Vân. It was discovered in January 2008 during the first flyby of the planet by MESSENGER spacecraft. Its floor displays an irregularly shaped collapse feature, which is called a central pit. The size of the pit is 21 × 10 km.

entries.title: Bek (crater)
entries.extract: Bek is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 32 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2010. Bek is named for the Egyptian sculptor Bek, who lived in the 14th century BCE.

entries.title: Dominici (crater)
entries.extract: Dominici is a crater on Mercury. It was named by the IAU in 2010.

entries.title: Geddes (crater)
entries.extract: Geddes is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 84 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2010. Geddes is named for the Irish stained glass artist Wilhelmina Geddes, who lived from 1887 to 1955.

entries.title: Hokusai (crater)
entries.extract: Hokusai is a rayed impact crater on Mercury, which was discovered in 1991 by ground-based radar observations conducted at Goldstone Observatory. The crater was initially known as feature B. Its appearance was so dissimilar to other impact craters that it was once thought to be a shield volcano.

entries.title: Picasso (crater)
entries.extract: Picasso is a crater on Mercury. It has drawn scientific attention because of the large, arc-shaped pit crater located on the eastern side of its floor. Similar pits have been discovered on the floors of several other Mercury craters, such as Beckett, Glinka, and Gibran.

entries.title: Kipling (crater)
entries.extract: Kipling is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 164 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2010. Kipling is named for the British author Rudyard Kipling, who lived from 1865 to 1936.

entries.title: Debussy (crater)
entries.extract: Debussy is a rayed impact crater on Mercury, which was discovered in 1969 by low resolution ground-based radar observations obtained by the Goldstone Observatory. Later in 1990–2005 it was imaged in more detail by the Arecibo Observatory. The crater was initially known as the feature A.

entries.title: Firdousi (crater)
entries.extract: Firdousi is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 98 km (61 mi). Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2010. Firdousi is named for the Persian poet Ferdowsi, who lived from 940 to 1020.

entries.title: Copland (crater)
entries.extract: Copland is an impact crater on Mercury. Its floor is flooded with volcanic smooth plains material, which could be related to the activity that formed the nearby bright vent known as Nathair Facula.

entries.title: Steichen (crater)
entries.extract: Steichen is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2010. The crater was named after American photographer and painter, Edward Steichen.

entries.title: Rachmaninoff (crater)
entries.extract: Rachmaninoff is an impact crater on Mercury. This basin, first imaged in its entirety during MESSENGER's third Mercury flyby, was quickly identified as a feature of high scientific interest, because of its fresh appearance, its distinctively colored interior plains, and the extensional troughs on its floor.

entries.title: Stieglitz (crater)
entries.extract: Stieglitz is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2012, after the American photographer Alfred Stieglitz.

entries.title: Ailey (crater)
entries.extract: Ailey is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 21 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in on April 24, 2012. Ailey is named for the American dancer and choreographer Alvin Ailey, who lived from 1931 to 1989.

entries.title: Aksakov (crater)
entries.extract: Aksakov is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 174 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on April 24, 2012. Aksakov is named for the Russian author Sergey Aksakov, who lived from 1791 to 1859 C.E.

entries.title: Balanchine (crater)
entries.extract: Balanchine is an impact crater on the planet Mercury. It possesses a ray system of slightly blue rays which inspired its name due to resembling the tutu in George Balanchine's Serenade.

entries.title: Lismer (crater)
entries.extract: Lismer is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 139.12 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on April 24, 2012. Lismer is named for the English-Canadian painter Arthur Lismer.

entries.title: Ellington (crater)
entries.extract: Ellington is a crater on Mercury named after Duke Ellington, an American composer, pianist, and leader of a jazz orchestra. It was named by the IAU in 2012.

entries.title: Faulkner (crater)
entries.extract: Faulkner is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 168 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on April 24, 2012. Faulkner is named for the American author William Faulkner.

entries.title: Fonteyn (crater)
entries.extract: Fonteyn is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the IAU in 2012, after the English ballet dancer Margot Fonteyn.

entries.title: Grainger (crater)
entries.extract: Grainger is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2012, after the Australian-born composer George Percy Aldridge Grainger.

entries.title: Grotell (crater)
entries.extract: Grotell is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 48.25 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on April 24, 2012. Grotell is named for the Finnish-American ceramist Maija Grotell.

entries.title: Henri (crater)
entries.extract: Henri is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 163.8 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on April 24, 2012. Henri is named for American painter Robert Henri.

entries.title: Holst (crater)
entries.extract: Holst is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on April 24, 2012.

entries.title: Kofi (crater)
entries.extract: Kofi is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 136 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on April 24, 2012. Kofi is named for the Ghanaian sculptor Vincent Kofi.

entries.title: Magritte (crater)
entries.extract: Magritte is a crater on Mercury, near the south pole. This crater was likely created by an impact event, as evident by its circular depression. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2012, after the Belgian painter, René Magritte.

entries.title: Mendelssohn (crater)
entries.extract: Mendelssohn is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on April 24, 2012. Mendelssohn is named for the German composer Jakob Ludwig Felix Mendelssohn.

entries.title: Nabokov (crater)
entries.extract: Nabokov is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on April 24, 2012. Nabokov is named for the Russian and American author Vladimir Nabokov.

entries.title: Nureyev (crater)
entries.extract: Nureyev is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 16 kilometers, and has a bright and extensive ray system. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Pasch (crater)
entries.extract: Pasch is a crater on Mercury, named by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2012 after Swedish painter Ulrika Pasch.

entries.title: Petipa (crater)
entries.extract: Petipa is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2012. It is named for the French and Russian choreographer and dancer Marius Petipa.

entries.title: Rustaveli (crater)
entries.extract: Rustaveli is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2012, after the Georgian poet Shota Rustaveli.

entries.title: Seuss (crater)
entries.extract: Seuss is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2012. It is named for the American author and cartoonist Theodor Seuss Geisel, better known as Dr. Seuss.

entries.title: Sousa (crater)
entries.extract: Sousa is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on April 24, 2012. Sousa is named for American bandmaster and composer John Philip Sousa.

entries.title: Stevenson (crater)
entries.extract: Stevenson is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2012, after the Scottish author Robert Louis Stevenson. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Warhol (crater)
entries.extract: Warhol is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the IAU in 2012, after the American artist Andy Warhol.

entries.title: Egonu (crater)
entries.extract: Egonu is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2012, after Nigerian artist Uzo Egonu.

entries.title: Gaudí (crater)
entries.extract: Gaudí is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2012, after the Spanish Catalan architect Antoni Gaudí.

entries.title: Kandinsky (crater)
entries.extract: Kandinsky is a deep crater on Mercury, located near the planet's north pole. It was named by the IAU in 2012 for Russian painter Wassily Kandinsky.

entries.title: Petronius (crater)
entries.extract: Petronius is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 36 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on the August 6, 2012. Petronius is named for the Roman author Petronius.

entries.title: Prokofiev (crater)
entries.extract: Prokofiev is a crater near the north pole of the planet Mercury, named after the Russian composer Sergei Prokofiev. Data from the MESSENGER spacecraft indicates that it contains water ice and organic compounds.

entries.title: Tolkien (crater)
entries.extract: 08 W. It is 50 km in diameter. It was named after the South African born British writer J. R. R. Tolkien. The name was approved by IAU's Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature on August 6, 2012.

entries.title: Tryggvadóttir (crater)
entries.extract: Tryggvadóttir is a crater on Mercury. The north pole of Mercury is located next to its northern rim. It was named by the IAU in 2012 after the Icelandic artist Nína Tryggvadóttir.

entries.title: Qiu Ying (crater)
entries.extract: Qiu Ying is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2012, for the Chinese painter Qiu Ying.

entries.title: Yoshikawa (crater)
entries.extract: Yoshikawa is a crater on Mercury, near the north pole. It was named by the IAU in 2012 after the Japanese novelist Eiji Yoshikawa.

entries.title: Chesterton (crater)
entries.extract: Chesterton is a crater on Mercury, near the north pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2012, after the English author G. K. Chesterton.

entries.title: Catullus (crater)
entries.extract: Catullus is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on December 19, 2012. Catullus is named for the Roman poet Catullus.

entries.title: Disney (crater)
entries.extract: Disney is an impact crater in the H-15 (Bach) Quadrangle of Mercury. It was approved and adopted by the IAU on Dec 19, 2012. Disney is 113 km (70 mi) in diameter. This crater was named after Walt Disney, the American entrepreneur, voice actor, film producer, and animator.

entries.title: Hopper (crater)
entries.extract: Hopper is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the IAU in 2012, after the American painter Edward Hopper. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Joplin (crater)
entries.extract: Joplin is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2012, after the American composer Scott Joplin.

entries.title: Kobro (crater)
entries.extract: Kobro is a crater near the south pole of the planet Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on the December 12, 2012. Kobro is named for the Polish sculptor Katarzyna Kobro. It is adjacent to Komeda crater, which was named at the same time.

entries.title: Komeda (crater)
entries.extract: Komeda is a crater near the south pole of the planet Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on the December 19, 2012. Komeda is named for the Polish composer Krzysztof Komeda. It is adjacent to Kobro crater, which was named at the same time.

entries.title: Kyōsai (crater)
entries.extract: Kyōsai is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2012. It is named for the Japanese artist Kawanabe Kyōsai.

entries.title: Popova (crater)
entries.extract: Popova is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2012, after the Russian painter and designer Lyubov Popova.

entries.title: Waters (crater)
entries.extract: Waters is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the IAU in 2012, after the American musician McKinley Morganfield, better known as Muddy Waters.

entries.title: Alver (crater)
entries.extract: Alver is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 151.49 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on March 15, 2013. Alver is named for the Estonian poet Betti Alver.

entries.title: Donelaitis (crater)
entries.extract: Donelaitis is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on May 15, 2013. Donelaitis is named for the Lithuanian poet Kristijonas Donelaitis.

entries.title: Flaiano (crater)
entries.extract: Flaiano is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 43 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on March 15, 2013. Flaiano is named for the Italian writer Ennio Flaiano. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Hurley (crater)
entries.extract: Hurley is a crater on Mercury, located near the south pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2013, after Australian photographer Frank Hurley.

entries.title: L'Engle (crater)
entries.extract: L'Engle is a crater on Mercury, located near the south pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2013, after American author Madeleine L'Engle.

entries.title: Lovecraft (crater)
entries.extract: Lovecraft is a crater on Mercury, located near the south pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2013, after American author Howard Phillips Lovecraft.

entries.title: Pahinui (crater)
entries.extract: Pahinui is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2016, after the Hawaiian musician, Charles Phillip Kahahawai "Gabby" Pahinui.

entries.title: Petőfi (crater)
entries.extract: Petőfi is a crater on Mercury, near the south pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2013, after the Hungarian poet Sándor Petőfi, following the official convention of naming craters on Mercury after historically significant artists, musicians, painters, and authors.

entries.title: Roerich (crater)
entries.extract: Roerich is a crater on Mercury, near the south pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2013, after the Russian painter Nicholas Roerich.

entries.title: Arecibo Catena
entries.extract: Arecibo Catena is a catena on Mercury. It is named after Arecibo Observatory, the former large radio telescope in Puerto Rico. It was originally named Arecibo Vallis, but the name was changed in 2013 to align with planetary feature naming themes.

entries.title: Goldstone Catena
entries.extract: Goldstone Catena is a catena on Mercury located at 15.8 S, 31.7 W. It is named after Goldstone Observatory. It was originally named Goldstone Vallis, but the name was changed in 2013 to align with planetary feature naming themes. While it superficially resembles a graben, it is a chain of overlapping secondary craters.

entries.title: Haystack Catena
entries.extract: Haystack Catena is a catena on Mercury. It superficially resembles a graben but is a chain of overlapping secondary craters.

entries.title: Belgica Rupes
entries.extract: Belgica Rupes is an escarpment in the Debussy quadrangle of Mercury. The escarpment is approximately 425 km long and cuts across the crater Carleton.

entries.title: Carnegie Rupes
entries.extract: Carnegie Rupes is an escarpment on Mercury, approximately 267 kilometers (166 mi) long, located at latitude 58.52 N and longitude 53.25 W. It was formed by a thrust fault, thought to have occurred due to the shrinkage of the planet's core as it cooled over time. The scarp cuts through Duccio crater.

entries.title: Enterprise Rupes
entries.extract: Enterprise Rupes is an escarpment on Mercury, located at 36.54°S, 283.46°W. It is the longest rupes on Mercury, with a length of 820 kilometers (510 mi). The escarpment was named after USS Enterprise, a ship which conducted the first surveys of the Mississippi and Amazon rivers.

entries.title: Duccio (crater)
entries.extract: Duccio is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on June 14, 2013. Duccio is named for the Italian painter Duccio di Buoninsegna.

entries.title: Bechet (crater)
entries.extract: Bechet is a crater on Mercury, located near the north pole. Most of the crater floor is in permanent shadow.

entries.title: Damer (crater)
entries.extract: Damer is a crater on Mercury in the Shakespeare quadrangle. Its diameter is 60 km. It was named after the English sculptor Anne Seymour Damer in 2013.

entries.title: David (crater)
entries.extract: David is a small crater on Mercury, which has a bright ray system. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2013. David is named for the French painter Jacques-Louis David.

entries.title: Erté (crater)
entries.extract: Erté is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2013. It is named for the artist and designer known as Erté.

entries.title: Larrocha (crater)
entries.extract: Larrocha is an impact crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 196 km (122 mi), and it is one of 110 peak ring basins on Mercury. It is located in the Victoria quadrangle at 43.29°N 69.83°W.

entries.title: Laxness (crater)
entries.extract: Laxness is a crater on Mercury, located near the north pole. It was named by the IAU in 2013, after Icelandic writer Halldór Laxness.

entries.title: Monk (crater)
entries.extract: Monk is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2013, after American jazz musician and composer Thelonious Monk.

entries.title: Rikyū (crater)
entries.extract: Rikyū is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on June 18, 2013. Rikyū is named for Japanese tea master and designer of the Japanese tea ceremony Sen no Rikyū.

entries.title: Varma (crater)
entries.extract: Varma is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on June 18, 2013. Varma is named for the Indian painter Raja Ravi Varma.

entries.title: Fuller (crater)
entries.extract: Fuller is a crater on Mercury, located near the north pole. It was named by the IAU in 2013, after American engineer and architect Richard Buckminster Fuller.

entries.title: Caravaggio (crater)
entries.extract: Caravaggio is a large crater on Mercury. The crater was named after the Italian painter Caravaggio by the IAU in 2013.

entries.title: Ruysch (crater)
entries.extract: Ruysch is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2013, and is named for the Netherland painter Rachel Ruysch.

entries.title: Savage (crater)
entries.extract: Savage is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2013, and is named for the American sculptor Augusta Savage.

entries.title: Barney (crater)
entries.extract: Barney is a small crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2013. Barney is named for the American-French playwright, poet, and novelist Natalie Clifford Barney.

entries.title: Berlioz (crater)
entries.extract: Berlioz is a crater on Mercury, located near the north pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2013. It is named for the French composer Hector Berlioz.

entries.title: Calder (crater)
entries.extract: Calder is a small crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2013. Calder is named for the American sculptor Alexander Calder.

entries.title: Capote (crater)
entries.extract: Capote is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2013, and is named for the American author Truman Capote.

entries.title: Caruso (crater)
entries.extract: Caruso is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on December 16, 2013. Caruso is named for the Italian singer Enrico Caruso. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974, but was not named at that time.

entries.title: Ensor (crater)
entries.extract: Ensor is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on December 16, 2013. Ensor is named for the Belgian painter James Ensor.

entries.title: Giambologna (crater)
entries.extract: Giambologna is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on December 16, 2013. Giambologna is named for the Flemish sculptor Jean Boulogne Giambologna. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Lennon (crater)
entries.extract: Lennon is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2013. Lennon is named for the English singer and songwriter John Lennon.

entries.title: Remarque (crater)
entries.extract: Remarque is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on December 16, 2013. Remarque is named for the German author Erich Maria Remarque.

entries.title: Vieira da Silva (crater)
entries.extract: Vieira da Silva is a large crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2013. The crater is named for the Portuguese abstract painter Maria Helena Vieira da Silva. The crater was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Kuniyoshi (crater)
entries.extract: Kuniyoshi is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2014. It is named for the Japanese painter and printmaker Utagawa Kuniyoshi.

entries.title: Aneirin (crater)
entries.extract: Aneirin is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 467 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on June 13, 2014. Aneirin is named for the Welsh poet Aneirin. Prior to naming, the crater was referred to as b37. It is Tolstojan in age.

entries.title: Hafiz (crater)
entries.extract: Hafiz is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 280 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on June 23, 2014. Hafiz is named for the Persian poet Hafez.

entries.title: Sanai (crater)
entries.extract: Sanai is a large, ancient crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2014, after the Persian poet, Sanai of Ghazna.

entries.title: Rivera (crater)
entries.extract: Rivera is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 40 kilometers. Its name was suggested by Mexican residents Ricardo Martinez and Arturo Gutierrez, and American residents Rebecca Hare and José Martinez, in a naming contest which was eventually adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on 2015.

entries.title: Carolan (crater)
entries.extract: Carolan is a crater on Mercury. Its name was suggested by an Irishman, Fergal Donnelly, and two Americans, Joseph Brusseau and Deane Morrison, in a naming contest which was eventually adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on 2015.E.

entries.title: Kulthum (crater)
entries.extract: Kulthum is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 31 kilometers.

entries.title: Enheduanna (crater)
entries.extract: Enheduanna is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 105 kilometers. Its name was suggested by Gagan Toor from India in a naming contest which was eventually adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on 2015. Enheduanna is named for the Sumerian poet Enheduanna.

entries.title: Karsh (crater)
entries.extract: Karsh is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 58 kilometers. Its name was suggested by American resident Elizabeth Freeman Rosenzweig in a naming contest which was eventually adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on 2015. Karsh is named for the Armenian-Canadian photographer Yousuf Karsh.

entries.title: Akutagawa (crater)
entries.extract: Akutagawa is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 106 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in on September 25, 2015. Akutagawa is named for the Japanese writer Ryūnosuke Akutagawa.

entries.title: Bagryana (crater)
entries.extract: Bagryana is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2017, after Bulgarian poet Elisaveta Bagryana.

entries.title: Baranauskas (crater)
entries.extract: Baranauskas is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 36 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on September 25, 2015. Baranauskas is named for the Lithuanian poet Antanas Baranauskas.

entries.title: Boznańska (crater)
entries.extract: Boznańska is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on September 25, 2015. Boznańska is named for the Polish painter Olga Boznańska.

entries.title: Brooks (crater)
entries.extract: Brooks is a crater on the southwestern part Mercury. It has a diameter of 34 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2015, and refers to the American poet and novelist Gwendolyn Brooks (1917–2000).

entries.title: Castiglione (crater)
entries.extract: Castiglione is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on September 25, 2015. Castiglione is named for the Italian painter Giuseppe Castiglione.

entries.title: Driscoll (crater)
entries.extract: Driscoll is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on September 25, 2015. Driscoll is named for the American stained glass artist Clara Driscoll.

entries.title: Jobim (crater)
entries.extract: Jobim is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 167 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on September 25, 2015. Jobim is named for the Brazilian composer Antônio Carlos Jobim.

entries.title: Namatjira (crater)
entries.extract: Namatjira is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 34 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on September 25, 2015. Namatjira is named for the Australian aboriginal artist Albert Namatjira.

entries.title: Plath (crater)
entries.extract: Plath is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2015. The crater is named for American poet Sylvia Plath.

entries.title: Du Fu (crater)
entries.extract: Du Fu is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on September 25, 2015. Du Fu is named for the Chinese poet Du Fu.

entries.title: Villa-Lobos (crater)
entries.extract: Villa-Lobos is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on September 25, 2015. Villa-Lobos is named for the Brazilian composer Heitor Villa-Lobos.

entries.title: Kerouac (crater)
entries.extract: Kerouac is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2015, after American author and poet Jack Kerouac.

entries.title: Burke (crater)
entries.extract: Burke is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on November 4, 2015. Burke is named for the American actress Billie Burke.

entries.title: Sapkota (crater)
entries.extract: Sapkota is a crater on Mercury, located near the north pole. It was named by the IAU in 2015, after Nepalese poet Mahananda Sapkota.

entries.title: Yamada (crater)
entries.extract: Yamada is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 17.1 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on November 4, 2015.
