Yamada is named for the Japanese composer and conductor Kosaku Yamada. The crater was referred to as n5 in scientific literature prior to naming.

entries.title: Otaared Planitia
entries.extract: Otaared Planitia is a smooth plain on Mercury. It was named for the Arabic word for the planet Mercury, in 2017 by the IAU. The plain is approximately 470 km (290 mi) in diameter.

entries.title: Apārangi Planitia
entries.extract: Apārangi Planitia is a large plain on Mercury, approximately 1077 km across. It was named in 2017 by the IAU.

entries.title: Sihtu Planitia
entries.extract: Sihtu Planitia is a large plain on Mercury, approximately 565 km across. It was named in 2017 by the IAU. The plain was first imaged by Mariner 10 in 1974.

entries.title: Stilbon Planitia
entries.extract: Stilbon Planitia is a large plain on the planet Mercury. The name Stilbon is ancient Greek word for "Mercury", and the name was approved in 2017. It was first observed in detail by MESSENGER. It lies north of the Caloris basin, and is approximately 1550 kilometers long.

entries.title: Mearcair Planitia
entries.extract: Mearcair Planitia is a large plain on the planet Mercury. The name Mearcair is the Irish and Scottish Gaelic word for "Mercury", and the name was approved in 2017. It was first observed in detail by MESSENGER. It lies between the large crater Raditladi and the ancient Caloris basin.

entries.title: Utaridi Planitia
entries.extract: Utaridi Planitia is a large plain in the southern hemisphere of Mercury. Most of it is in the Debussy quadrangle, but it extends to the east into Neruda quadrangle and to the south into Bach quadrangle. The plain was named by the IAU in 2017.

entries.title: Heaney (crater)
entries.extract: Heaney is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 125 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on March 20, 2017. Heaney is named for the Irish poet and playwright Seamus Heaney.

entries.title: Anguissola (crater)
entries.extract: Anguissola is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 35.41 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on August 4, 2017. Anguissola is named for the Italian painter Sofonisba Anguissola.

entries.title: Anyte (crater)
entries.extract: Anyte is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 20.92 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on August 4, 2017. Anyte is named for the Greek poet Anyte of Tegea.

entries.title: Vonnegut (crater)
entries.extract: Vonnegut is a crater on Mercury, near the north pole. It was named by the IAU in 2017 after the American author Kurt Vonnegut. Part of Vonnegut's 1959 novel The Sirens of Titan takes place on Mercury. The crater was referred to as e5 in scientific literature prior to naming.

entries.title: Nathair Facula
entries.extract: Nathair Facula is a bright region on the surface of Mercury, located at 36° N, 295.5° W. It was named by the IAU in 2018. Nathair is the Irish and Scottish Gaelic word for snake.

entries.title: Neidr Facula
entries.extract: Neidr Facula is a bright, irregular depression on the surface of Mercury, located at 35.9° N, 302.7° W. It was named by the IAU in 2018. Neidr is the Welsh word for snake.

entries.title: Suge Facula
entries.extract: Suge Facula is a bright region on the surface of Mercury, located at 26.1 N, 300.4 W. It was named by the IAU in 2018. Suge is the Basque word for snake.

entries.title: Agwo Facula
entries.extract: Agwo Facula is a bright, irregular depression on the surface of Mercury, located at 22.4° N, 213.7° W, in southwestern Caloris Planitia. It was named by the IAU in 2018. Agwo is the Igbo word for snake. The depression is the site of multiple volcanic explosions.

entries.title: Abeeso Facula
entries.extract: Abeeso Facula is a bright, irregular depression on the surface of Mercury, located at 21.7° N, 214.6° W, in southwestern Caloris Planitia. It was named by the IAU in 2018. Abeeso is the Somali word for snake. The depression is the site of a volcanic explosion.

entries.title: Slang Faculae
entries.extract: Slang Faculae is a bright region on the surface of Mercury, located at 24.5° N, 179.3° W. It was named by the IAU in 2018. Slang is the Afrikaans word for snake.

entries.title: Nākahi Facula
entries.extract: Nākahi Facula is a bright, irregular depression on the surface of Mercury, located at 52.7° S, 342.2° W. It was named by the IAU in 2018. Nākahi is the Māori word for snake.

entries.title: Amaru Facula
entries.extract: Amaru Facula is a bright, irregular depression on the surface of Mercury, located at 49.8° S, 349.5° W. It was named by the IAU in 2018. Amaru is the Quechua word for snake.

entries.title: Canova (crater)
entries.extract: Canova is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2018, after Italian sculptor Antonio Canova.

entries.title: Travers (crater)
entries.extract: Travers is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2018, after the British writer Pamela Lyndon Travers.

entries.title: Carleton (crater)
entries.extract: Carleton is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on October 19, 2018. Carleton is named for the Irish writer William Carleton.

entries.title: Bellini (crater)
entries.extract: Bellini is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2019, and is named for the Italian painter Giovanni Bellini.

entries.title: Pampu Facula
entries.extract: Pampu Facula is a bright region on the surface of Mercury, located at 57.76° S, 31.79° W. It was named by the IAU in 2019. Pampu is the Tamil word for snake.

entries.title: Ular Facula
entries.extract: Ular Facula is a bright region on the surface of Mercury, located at 55.1° S, 29.95° W. It was named by the IAU in 2019. Ular is the Malay word for snake.

entries.title: Sarpa Facula
entries.extract: Sarpa Facula is a bright region on the surface of Mercury, located at 53.07° S, 30.87° W. It was named by the IAU in 2019. Sarpa is the Sinhalese word for snake.

entries.title: Martins (crater)
entries.extract: Martins is a small crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2019. Martins is named for the Brazilian sculptor Maria Martins.

entries.title: Angelou (crater)
entries.extract: Angelou is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 18 kilometers. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on September 11, 2019. Angelou is named for the American poet and author Maya Angelou.

entries.title: Josetsu (crater)
entries.extract: Josetsu is a crater on Mercury, located near the north pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2019. It is named for the Japanese painter Taikō Josetsu. The crater was referred to as o7 in scientific literature prior to naming.

entries.title: Rizal (crater)
entries.extract: Rizal is a crater on Mercury, located near the north pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2019. It is named for the Filipino writer José Rizal.

entries.title: Jiménez (crater)
entries.extract: Jiménez is a crater on Mercury, located near the north pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2019. It is named for the Spanish poet and author Juan Ramón Jiménez.

entries.title: Kirby (crater)
entries.extract: Kirby is a crater on Mercury, located near the north pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2019. It is named for the American illustrator Jack Kirby.

entries.title: Bunin (crater)
entries.extract: Bunin is a crater on Mercury, located near the north pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2019. It is named for the Russian author Ivan Bunin. The crater was referred to as l7 in scientific literature prior to naming.

entries.title: Strauss (crater)
entries.extract: Strauss is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2019, after the Strauss family of musicians.

entries.title: Gordimer (crater)
entries.extract: Gordimer is a crater on Mercury, near the north pole. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2019, after the South African writer Nadine Gordimer.

entries.title: Zmija Facula
entries.extract: Zmija Facula is a bright region on the surface of Mercury, located within an unnamed crater that is itself within the larger Rembrandt basin. It was named by the IAU in June 2020. Zmija is the Serbian word for snake.

entries.title: Coatl Facula
entries.extract: Coatl Facula is a bright region about 49 km wide on the surface of Mercury, located at 29.75° S, 216.55° W. It was named by the IAU in June 2020. Coatl is the Aztec (Nahuatl) word for snake.

entries.title: Wen Tianxiang (crater)
entries.extract: Wen Tianxiang is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in June 2020, and it is named for Chinese writer and poet Wen Tianxiang.

entries.title: Vazov (crater)
entries.extract: Vazov is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2020. The crater is named for Bulgarian poet Ivan Vazov.

entries.title: Berry (crater)
entries.extract: Berry is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on September 28, 2020. Berry is named for the American singer and songwriter Chuck Berry.

entries.title: Veronese (crater)
entries.extract: Veronese is a crater on Mercury. It has a diameter of 45 kilometres. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on June 28, 2021. Veronese is named for the Italian painter Paolo Veronese.

entries.title: Nairne (crater)
entries.extract: Nairne is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2022. The crater is named for Scottish songwriter Carolina Nairne.

entries.title: Lorde (crater)
entries.extract: Lorde is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2022. The crater is named for American poet Audre Lorde.

entries.title: MacNicol (crater)
entries.extract: MacNicol is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 2022. MacNicol is named for the Scottish painter Bessie MacNicol, who lived from 1869 to 1904.

entries.title: Morrison (crater)
entries.extract: Morrison is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union in September 2022. Morrison is named for the American author Toni Morrison, who lived from 1931 to 2019.

entries.title: Zapiola Rupes
entries.extract: Zapiola Rupes is an escarpment on Mercury. The escarpment was named after Zapiola, the eponymous Argentine ship that was involved in oceanographic surveys in the southwestern Atlantic; and performed ten oceanographic cruises between 1962 and 1976.

entries.title: Manley (crater)
entries.extract: Manley is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2023, for the Jamaican sculptor, painter, and printmaker Edna Manley, who lived from 1900 to 1987.

entries.title: Bulsara (crater)
entries.extract: Bulsara is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in May 2024, for British musician Farrokh Bulsara, better known as Freddie Mercury, lead vocalist and pianist of the rock band Queen, who lived from 1946 to 1991.

entries.title: Sontag (crater)
entries.extract: Sontag is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on August 13, 2024, for the American novelist and essayist Susan Sontag, who lived from 1933 to 2004.

entries.title: Piazzolla (crater)
entries.extract: Piazzolla is a crater on Mercury. Its name was adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) on August 13, 2024, for the Argentine tango composer and bandoneon player Astor Piazzolla, who lived from 1921 to 1992.
